string-array.item: ATSC 8-VSB, 6 MHz channel (the DVB-only settings are off)
ATSC 3.0 (NextGen TV), 6 MHz channel, ROUTE services
ISDB-T (Japan, Brazil and most of South America; 8 MHz channels in the Maldives), 6, 7 or 8 MHz channel, 13 segments
DVB-S, DVB-S2 and DVB-S2X satellite TV (L-band IF through an LNB)
DTMB / DTMB-A digital TV (China, Hong Kong, Cuba), 8 or 6 MHz channel
DVB-C cable TV (EN 300 429 / J.83 annex A and C): 16 to 256-QAM, symbol rate measured or set; needs a cable feed
Analogue TV: PAL, SECAM and NTSC with FM, NICAM-728 or A2 stereo sound
MAC television (D2-MAC, D-MAC): the 1980s-90s European satellite TV, FM, about 27 MHz wide (20 Msps sees most of it)
DAB / DAB+ digital radio, Band III channels 5A to 13F
FM broadcast radio (87.5 - 108 MHz), stereo and RDS
DRM30 and DRM+ digital radio (shortwave, medium wave, VHF)
HD Radio (NRSC-5) digital sidebands of FM and AM stations (USA)
CDR (China Digital Radio) OFDM digital radio in the FM band
ADS-B / Mode S: aircraft on 1090 MHz
Mode S uplink: the 1030 MHz interrogations of radars and ACAS (Mode A/C, intermode, UF0 to UF24); needs 8 Msps
ACARS aircraft data link messages around 131 MHz

VDL Mode 2: the aircraft data link on 136.725 to 136.975 MHz, every channel at once. Every frame of the session is kept with its UTC date and time and can be saved as CSV, JSON or text; under Advanced the bandwidth and the sample rate can be set to anything (Custom)
HFDL: the HF aircraft data link (ARINC 635), 3 to 22 MHz, every channel in the band at once
Airband AM voice, 118 to 137 MHz: several 25 and 8.33 kHz channels at once; also the military UHF air band, 225 to 400 MHz (25 kHz channels, 243.000 guard)
VOR navigation beacons, 108 to 118 MHz: the radial, the identification and a position from two stations
ILS approach guidance: localizer 108.10 - 111.95 MHz, glide slope 329 - 335 MHz, marker beacons on 75 MHz

NDB (non-directional beacon) on long wave, 190-535 kHz: the Morse ident of an aeronautical beacon (a keyed 400 Hz or 1020 Hz tone, or a keyed carrier, about 7 WPM). Receive only. Not the HF beacon list

Drone Remote ID (ASTM F3411 / ASD-STAN EN 4709-002 Open Drone ID) on 2.4 GHz: Bluetooth LE advertising and Wi-Fi beacons at once; serial number or session ID, UA type, position, height, speed and track, operator position and ID, on a table and a map (receive only: Remote ID is a public broadcast meant for anyone to read; nothing is transmitted)
AIS ship transponders on 161.975 and 162.025 MHz

VDES (VHF Data Exchange System, ITU-R M.2092): ASM messages on 161.950 / 162.000 MHz decoded (GMSK 9.6 kbit/s, AIS framing, CRC checked); AIS-like frames show their position, on the Map tab and as !AIVDM sentences over UDP for a chart program (the AIS data feed); VDE-TER bursts on the 157.2 and 161.8 MHz channels detected with bandwidth, level and modulation class (frames not decoded)
NAVTEX navigational and weather warnings to ships, 518 kHz (SITOR-B)
DSC digital selective calling: distress alerts and calls, MF/HF and VHF channel 70
HF weather fax (radiofax): weather charts for ships on upper sideband
GNSS satellites (GPS, GLONASS, BeiDou, Galileo) around 1575 MHz, needs an active antenna
Inmarsat-C satellite messages (EGC safety and news broadcasts) near 1537.7 MHz
Inmarsat Aero satellite data link: P channels at 600 and 1200 bit/s near 1545 MHz, and 10500 bit/s near 1546 MHz
Meteor-M N2-3 / N2-4 weather pictures on 137.1 / 137.9 MHz (LRPT: OQPSK or QPSK, 72 or 80 ksym/s): the MSU-MR channels and a colour composite grow line by line during the pass, saved as PNG

GOES-16 / 18 / 19 HRIT on 1694.1 MHz (BPSK 927 ksym/s, Viterbi, Reed-Solomon, CCSDS packets, LRIT files): full disk and mesoscale images (Rice, plain or JPEG) grow as their lines arrive, EMWIN weather text and admin messages, saved to a folder. Needs a dish (about 1 m, or a grid) with an LNA at the feed

Elektro-L N3 / N4 / N5 L-band weather: HRIT and LRIT on 1691 MHz (BPSK, Viterbi, Reed-Solomon, CCSDS / xRIT, the same product path as GOES) and GGAK space-weather PCM/PM on 1693 MHz at 5 ksym/s. Pick the spacecraft and the link. Needs a dish with an LNA. Receive only

HRPT / AHRPT weather satellite pictures near 1.7 GHz: MetOp-B / MetOp-C AHRPT (QPSK 2.33 Msym/s, 1701.3 MHz) with the AVHRR channels growing line by line, FY-3 AHRPT as frame counts only (the FY-3 satellites have their own modes, FY-3 AHRPT and FY-3 MPT, with the pictures) and the retired NOAA HRPT (BPSK, Manchester, 665.4 kbit/s). Needs a dish (about 1 m or more, tracking the satellite) with an LNA at the feed and a fast radio (4 Msps or more: HackRF, Airspy, SDRplay, Pluto; not an RTL-SDR)
Orbcomm subscriber downlinks, 137.2 - 137.8 MHz: 4800 bit/s SDPSK, two downlinks at once, satellites and their ephemeris

QO-100 (Es\'hail-2) geostationary amateur satellite, 10489.5 - 10500 MHz through a Ku LNB: beacon lock corrects the LNB\'s error and drift, narrowband SSB listening, wideband DATV hand-over to DVB-S/S2

FLARM: glider and light-aircraft collision-avoidance broadcasts on 868.2 and 868.4 MHz (Europe), received like the Open Glider Network does. Old-protocol positions are decoded (device ID, type, altitude, speed, track, climb) and shown in a table and on the live map with distance and bearing from your receiver; the newer protocol is only counted. Receive only; aircraft that set the no-track or stealth flag are only counted, never shown or saved

DJI drones on 2.4 and 5.8 GHz, receive only: wideband OFDM burst trains are classified by their shape (OcuSync-like, Lightbridge-like, unknown wideband OFDM) from the width, burst period, duty cycle and cyclic-prefix correlation, with a confidence and a clear note that this is a guess from the signal shape; DJI DroneID (the OcuSync 2 broadcast: Zadoff-Chu roots 600 and 147, turbo code, CRC-24) is decoded to the drone\'s serial number, position, home point and pilot position as sent in the clear. Needs 16 Msps or more (HackRF at 20 Msps; Pluto, bladeRF, USRP). The encrypted video link is never decoded

CubeSat telemetry from amateur satellites on 2 m / 70 cm (145.8 - 146 and 435 - 438 MHz): AX.25 at 1200 baud AFSK and 9600 baud G3RUH, GOMspace AX100 Mode 5 (ASM + Golay + Reed-Solomon) and Mode 6, CCSDS Reed-Solomon frames, GOMspace U482C (AFSK), CCSDS concatenated (Viterbi + RS), SPUTNIX USP, NGHam and Mobitex / BEESAT; callsigns, hex and ASCII dumps, satellite names from an editable table, KISS out to SatNOGS-style tools; the pass planner starts it with Doppler and sets the framing and baud rate from the gr-satellites satellite table. AX100 Mode 5, AX100 Mode 6, USP, NGHam, U482C and BEESAT / Mobitex also have a mode-list entry of their own (the same decoder, one framing each)

Globalstar L-band terminal uplink (mobile to satellite), 1610 - 1626.5 MHz; the satellite downlink is S-band 2483.5 - 2500 MHz and is not tuned. Activity monitor only (receive only, the spread and encrypted content is not decoded): power, occupancy and Doppler of the 13 CDMA channels, an event log, and a pass overlay from the pass planner\'s TLEs
DMR two-slot digital voice and data, 12.5 kHz channel
NXDN digital two-way radio: NXDN48 (6.25 kHz) and NXDN96 (12.5 kHz), conventional and trunked
APCO Project 25 Phase 1 (TIA-102) digital two-way radio, C4FM, 12.5 kHz: conventional channels and trunked control channels
dPMR (ETSI TS 102 490) digital two-way radio, 6.25 kHz: PMR446 digital channels 1 to 16 (446.1 - 446.2 MHz) and the licensed bands

TETRA base stations (ETSI EN 300 392): network code, colour code, location area, carriers, neighbour cells, services and whether encryption is used (receive only, public broadcast, nothing decrypted). Under Advanced, the bandwidth and the sample rate can be set to anything (Custom): a wide capture on a HackRF at 10 to 20 Msps lists and decodes every carrier of the 380 - 400 MHz range it covers

TETRAPOL (not TETRA), GMSK 8 kbit/s on 10 / 12.5 kHz channels (PAS 0001-2), polarity found automatically: D_SYSTEM_INFO gives country, system, cell, location area and scramble; clear calls play through your own codec plug-in, encrypted calls are never decoded. Under Advanced, the bandwidth and the sample rate can be set to anything (Custom); the carrier at the tuned frequency is decoded
LTE cells around you: operator, band, EARFCN, PCI, eNB and sector, TAC, neighbours (receive only, public broadcast)

5G NR cells around you from their SS/PBCH blocks on the sync raster (GSCN) of n1, n3, n7, n8, n20, n28, n38, n40, n41, n77, n78: PCI, SSB index / beam, SS-RSRP / RSRQ / SINR, MIB (SFN, subcarrier spacing, k_SSB, CORESET#0, barred) (receive only, public broadcast)

LTE NB-IoT cells around you (180 kHz carriers, in-band, guard band or standalone) from their NPSS / NSSS, NPBCH (MIB-NB) and SIB1-NB: PCI, operating mode, antenna ports, SFN, operator (MCC / MNC), tracking area, cell identity, band, level; band scan over the 100 kHz raster. Receive only: the public broadcast only, nothing addressed to a device is decoded

GSM base stations, railway GSM-R (921 - 925 MHz) and the public GSM 850 / 900, DCS 1800 and PCS 1900 bands: cell identity, location area, operator, channel lists, GPRS and 3G / 4G neighbour indications, and the paging / access load of the common control channel (message kinds only). Receive only, public broadcast
LBJ (Chinese railway train proximity warning) on about 821.2375 MHz: FM voice channel with 1200 bit/s FSK data for train number, kilometre marker, locomotive ID, direction and speed (receive only)
POCSAG paging messages (512, 1200 and 2400 bd) on a 25 kHz channel
FLEX paging messages (1600, 3200 and 6400 bit/s) on a 25 kHz channel
Everyday 315, 345, 433.92, 868 and 915 MHz devices: weather stations, tyre pressure sensors, remotes, energy and water meters, Z-Wave (passive; S0 and S2 stay encrypted)

LoRaWAN monitor, EU868 (868.1 / 868.3 / 868.5 MHz) or US915, SF7 - SF12: message types, DevAddr and network, frame counters, MAC commands, join requests (only the clear headers; payloads stay encrypted)
Meshtastic LoRa mesh messages, positions and telemetry (868 and 915 MHz bands)
MeshCore LoRa mesh adverts and messages (868 and 915 MHz bands)
Bluetooth Low Energy advertising on channels 37, 38 and 39 (2402 / 2426 / 2480 MHz): device names, vendors, services, iBeacon and Eddystone, like a scanner app (receive only: never connects or pairs)

Zigbee and IEEE 802.15.4 on the 2.4 GHz channels 11 - 26 (O-QPSK, 2 Mchip/s, 250 kbit/s): networks (PAN ID, extended PAN ID, coordinator), devices with vendor from the address, MAC / NWK / APS headers, beacons and commands, a live frame log; channel scan. Receive only: encrypted payloads are not decrypted (the network key is not obtainable), only frames sent in the clear are shown. Needs a fast radio (4 Msps or more), not an RTL-SDR

Wi-Fi HaLow (802.11ah) networks in the sub-GHz bands of ten regions (863 - 868 MHz in Europe, 902 - 928 MHz in the US and Canada, Japan, Korea, Singapore, Australia, New Zealand, China, India, Taiwan): S1G beacons at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 MHz channel widths (S1G_1M, S1G_SHORT and S1G_LONG preambles, MCS 0 - 10) give the SSID, BSSID, vendor, channel, width, MCS, streams, SNR, level and the security type the network announces (information only). Region and channel lists with operating classes, auto-detect or manual width, a channel scan. Receive only: nothing is sent or joined and nothing is decrypted. 1 and 2 MHz channels work from 2.4 Msps (an RTL-SDR), 4 MHz from 4 Msps, 8 MHz from 10 Msps, 16 MHz from 20 Msps

Datawell Waverider wave-buoy telemetry on HF, 25.5 - 35.5 MHz (up to 45 MHz on request), heard as a USB signal. The 2FSK format of the DWR-MkIII, DWR-G and WR-SG buoys (81.92 bit/s) is decoded from Datawell\'s published reference manual: heave / north / west displacements, wave height and period, water temperature, GPS position and the 64 band directional spectrum, with the buoy\'s error-correcting code repairing bit errors. The 4FSK format of the DWR4 (163.84 bit/s) is not public: only the carrier, its tones and measurements of the bit stream are shown. Listed channel presets. Receive only

CODAR SeaSonde, WERA and similar coastal HF ocean radars: the FMCW sweeps in the 4.4 - 4.65, 5.25, 12 - 14, 24.45 - 24.65 and 41.5 - 42.5 MHz bands, found as moving lines in the spectrum: centre, sweep width, rate, direction, repetition and level, a table of the radars heard with first / last heard and SNR history, a chirp waterfall with the sweeps marked, the band and time each was heard (propagation, no position claimed), band presets and a scan over the radar bands. The Morse call sign some radars send is decoded from the keyed sweep width and always labelled unverified. Receive only: broadcast radar, nothing is decrypted

Multitone Electronics (UK) pagers, Mk IV to VII, in hospitals and industrial sites, 25 - 470 MHz, narrowband FM with FFSK: a detector, not a decoder, because the format is not public. Per transmission: the carrier, the FM deviation, the steady tones and spectral lines of the audio and, when the audio is two-level FSK, the measured baud rate, the bit stream in hex and how many 32-bit words pass the POCSAG BCH(31,21) check, with the POCSAG sync word flagged. Everything is labelled unverified; no message text is shown. Receive only: pager messages are private, nothing is decrypted or transmitted

NOAA Weather Radio (US and Canada) SAME / EAS alerts on the seven narrow-FM weather channels, 162.400 - 162.550 MHz: the 520.83 baud AFSK header sent three times is voted bit by bit and every field checked, then shown in plain English: originator, event (tornado warning, severe thunderstorm warning, required weekly test and the rest of the EAS table), the locations with the partial-county direction, valid for, issue time and sender call sign, how many of the three repeats agreed, the 1050 Hz attention tone, an alert history and a map of the states and provinces named (approximate). County names come only from a county table you load (none are built in). Receive only: the text of an alert is a public broadcast

ANT+ sensors on 2457 MHz (and other ANT networks on their own channel): heart rate straps and watches, bike speed, cadence and power sensors, footpods, environment sensors, as a watch or bike computer hears them: 1 Mbit/s GFSK frames with the device number, type and the data page, the heart rate with the beat count and R-R interval plotted over time, power, cadence, speed, temperature, manufacturer, serial and battery pages. Receive only: nothing is sent, paired or acknowledged, and only the open broadcasts are shown. Needs a radio that reaches 2.4 GHz at 4 Msps (HackRF, Pluto, LimeSDR, BladeRF, USRP).

DECT cordless phones and base stations on the ten carriers 1881.792 - 1897.344 MHz (Europe; 1.152 Mbit/s GFSK, 10 ms frames of 24 slots): every base station from the beacon it sends every frame, with its RFPI (the manufacturer code and system number inside it), level and the slots it uses, the system information tails and a burst log with base and handset bursts. Activity and signalling only: calls are encrypted and the voice is not decoded, nothing is transmitted. Needs a radio that reaches 1.9 GHz at 5 Msps or more (HackRF, Pluto, LimeSDR, BladeRF, USRP, SDRplay).

Plain LoRa between two radios (point to point, not LoRaWAN, not a mesh): every frame as bytes (hex and text) with SNR, level and carrier offset. You set the spreading factor (SF5 - SF12), bandwidth (125 / 250 / 500 kHz), coding rate and CRC (implicit header), header mode and sync word, or leave the spreading factor and bandwidth on Auto and every combination is searched. EU868, US915 and 433 MHz presets. Receive only: nothing is sent, decrypted or interpreted

Wi-Fi access points on 2.4 GHz (channels 1 - 14, 802.11b and OFDM beacons), 5 GHz (channels 36 - 177, UNII-1 to UNII-4 with DFS) and 6 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E / 7, channels 1 - 233, FILS discovery and unsolicited probe responses) from their beacons: SSID, BSSID and vendor, band, channel, width, standard (a / n / ac / ax / be), security (open, WEP, WPA, WPA2, WPA3, OWE, key management, protected management frames), capabilities, BSS color, co-located 6 GHz APs from the Reduced Neighbor Report and level, with a band selector, channel scan and channel occupancy chart. Needs 20 Msps for a 20 MHz channel (passive: beacons only, never joins or transmits)
Weather balloon radiosondes, 400 to 406 MHz (RS41, DFM, M10 and others)

Time and frequency stations: DCF77 (77.5 kHz), MSF and WWVB (60 kHz), JJY (40 / 60 kHz), WWV / WWVH (2.5 - 20 MHz): the time, date, summer time and leap second flags, the seconds tick, and how far the computer clock is off after the path delay

HF chirp sounders (ionosondes and oblique sounders, 0 - 30 MHz at 100 - 500 kHz/s): sweeps found by dechirping, their rate, period and start offset, an ionogram of group range against frequency, a timeline, PNG / CSV export; no decoder
Radio astronomy: the 21 cm hydrogen line (1420.4058 MHz) and the OH lines; long integration, on - off reference, baseline fit, radial velocity, drift-scan waterfall, CSV export; no decoder
FT8 weak-signal contacts in 15 s slots, 14.074 MHz
FT4 contest mode in 7.5 s slots, 14.080 MHz
WSPR propagation beacons in 2 minute slots, 14.0956 MHz
JT65 weak-signal contacts (65-FSK, Reed-Solomon, 60 s periods, sub-modes A, B, C), 14.076 MHz
JT9 weak-signal contacts (9-FSK, convolutional code, 60 s periods, 15 Hz wide), 14.078 MHz
Q65 (A to E, 15 s to 5 min periods) for EME, scatter and weak-signal work: Q-ary repeat-accumulate code, 65-FSK
FST4 and FST4W (15 s to 30 min periods, 4-GFSK, LDPC (240,101) / (240,74)) for LF, MF and HF weak-signal contacts and beacons
MSK144 meteor scatter (72 ms frames, 2000 baud, 15 s periods): decodes the short bursts of meteor trails
PSK31 / PSK63 keyboard chat (BPSK and QPSK): every signal in the 3 kHz passband at once, 14.070 MHz
JS8Call keyboard messaging (8-FSK, normal / fast / turbo slots): heartbeats, directed messages, relays, 14.078 MHz
RTTY teletype (45.45 bd, 170 Hz shift) on upper sideband, 1 to 30 MHz
CW (Morse) skimmer: every signal in a 14 kHz window, 5 to 50 WPM, on the HF CW segments
SSTV slow-scan TV pictures (Martin, Scottie, Robot, PD) on upper sideband
HamDRM / EasyPal digital SSTV: pictures as files over DRM-style OFDM in 2.3 or 2.5 kHz of upper sideband, 14.233 MHz
Olivia MFSK keyboard mode with Walsh-Hadamard coding, weak-signal text, 14.1065 MHz
Contestia (Olivia with 6-bit characters, upper case, faster), 14.1095 MHz
MFSK4 to MFSK128 keyboard modes (MFSK16 is the usual one) with forward error correction, 14.0785 MHz; MFSK16 / 32 / 64 / 128 also show the pictures of Shortwave Radiogram
THOR keyboard modes (4 to 100) with incremental frequency keying and FEC, 14.077 MHz
DominoEX keyboard modes (4 to 22) with incremental frequency keying, 14.0715 MHz
Hellschreiber (Feld Hell, Slow Hell, Hell 80, HellX5): text as a picture of dots, 14.063 MHz
FreeDV digital voice (700D, 700E, 1600) on upper sideband
M17 open digital voice and data (4FSK, 9 kHz), 2 m and 70 cm
D-STAR digital voice (GMSK 4800 bit/s, 6.25 kHz), 2 m and 70 cm
APRS and AX.25 packet radio (1200 bd AFSK), 144.800 MHz in Europe; LoRa APRS is its own entry
LoRa APRS on 70 cm, 433.775 MHz in Europe (SF12, 125 kHz)
MeshCom LoRa nodes on 70 cm, 433.175 MHz in Europe
HF ALE (2G, MIL-STD-188-141 / FED-STD-1045): 8-FSK link establishment calls, soundings, AMD messages and LQA on the HFN channels, 14.109 MHz

HF beacon propagation monitor: which NCDXF/IARU International Beacon Project beacons (18 beacons on 14.100, 18.110, 21.150, 24.930 and 28.200 MHz, 10 s slots), Australian Long Dashes and Russian single-letter beacons can be heard from here, by band, with SNR, distance and bearing, a great-circle map and 24 hour history; an editable beacon list; clicking a beacon tunes and listens

Open a recording (WAV, MP3 or other audio, or an IQ file: .cs8 .cu8 .cf32 .sigmf) and take the signal apart without a radio: waveform and spectrogram with cursors, peaks, bandwidth, SNR, symbol rate, bursts and a modulation guess, then demodulate a chosen band (AM, FM, SSB, CW, ASK, FSK, AFSK, PSK, MSK) and read the bits
Listen anywhere in the band: NFM, WFM (mono), AM, USB, LSB and CW, click the spectrum to tune, filter width, squelch, AGC, de-emphasis, S-meter and audio recording to WAV
Spectrum explorer: look around the band, measure carriers (bandwidth, power, SNR, symbol rate), sweep a range, LNB offsets, bookmarks; no decoder
Wide sweeping spectrum analyser (1 - 6000 MHz in about a second with a HackRF): live, peak-hold and averaged traces, waterfall, markers, band overlay, CSV export
Finds out which TV standard the channel carries (DVB-T, DVB-T2, DVB-C, DVB-S/S2, ISDB-T, ATSC 1.0 / 3.0, DTMB, analogue) and its parameters, then switches the receiver on

Television streamed over the internet: add an M3U / M3U8 playlist (a web address or a file) or open one stream address (HLS, MPEG-TS over HTTP, UDP or RTP, also multicast); channel list with logos, groups, search and favourites, programme guide (XMLTV), and the same player as the antenna TV: volume, subtitles, audio track, full screen, recording. No radio is needed. OnAir comes with no channels and plays no DRM protected streams

TV satellite beacon decoder: the narrow carrier of a geostationary satellite (a Ku or Ka band beacon through an LNB), found anywhere in the capture and followed in frequency and level (C/N0, offset, drift per minute), the other narrow lines and a second reference carrier listed with their spacing. A phase-modulated beacon is demodulated too: the telemetry tones are found, the BPSK bits recovered at the detected bit rate, and the frame length, frame start and the bits that never change learned from the repetition; frames are listed in hex, their words classified (constants, counters, a clock, a checksum, commutated words, samples) and shown in a decoded view that can be exported as CSV or JSON; the satellite is estimated from the frequency against a table of published beacons. The frame layout of a given satellite is not decoded. Needs a radio that sees the beacon (an LNB and a dish, 2 Msps or more)
ISDB-S, Japanese BS satellite television (12 GHz through an LNB): 28.86 Msym/s, BPSK / QPSK / TC8PSK slots, TMCC, Reed-Solomon; needs a radio that samples 39 Msps or more
Analog FPV video links (drones, 5.8 GHz bands A, B, E, F, R, L and 1.2 GHz): scan the channels, watch the picture live, record it
AM broadcast on medium wave and shortwave (the general receiver in AM, with MW and SW presets)

AM stereo, C-QUAM (Motorola) on medium wave: the 25 Hz pilot found, left and right from the phase of the carrier, a stereo / mono indicator and the audio on the sound card; plain AM stations play as mono

Mode A / C transponder replies on 1090 MHz: the squawk (Mode A, four octal digits) and the altitude (Mode C, 100 ft steps) of aircraft that answer secondary radar, with the ident pulse, shown beside the Mode S aircraft of the same capture on the ADS-B map and matched to them by squawk or altitude. Needs the same radio as ADS-B (2 Msps or more, 4 Msps recommended)
VDL Mode 4: STDMA GFSK data link on 118 to 137 MHz (synthetic + spec; receive only)

Marine VHF voice, channels 1 to 88 at 156 to 162 MHz: narrow FM with squelch, a channel picker with names and uses (16 distress, 70 DSC, 13 bridge to bridge ...), up / down, scan with a priority watch on 16, every channel of the span at once with an activity list, a call log and a recording per channel

SELCAL (ARINC 714), the two-pair tone call that alerts an aircraft\'s crew on an HF or VHF airband voice channel: 16 tones from 312.6 to 1479.1 Hz, two pairs of one second, written as four letters such as AM-CP. Every call is logged with the time, the four tone frequencies, the dial frequency and the aircraft when its code is in your own table (selcal_aircraft.tsv). A code names an airframe and carries no position, so there is no map. Tune an aeronautical HF channel (USB, for example 8.891 MHz) or a VHF airband channel (AM)

ATIS, the Automatic Transmitter Identification System of the European inland waterways (Rhine, Danube, Rhone ...; not AIS): a VHF radio sends its ten digit identity by itself when the operator lets go of the push-to-talk key, 1200 baud FSK with 1300 and 2100 Hz tones in the DSC code (ETSI EN 300 698-1 annex B). The voice of the channel plays as narrow FM, the identity is decoded, checked and listed with the country, the call sign it spells and the ship name when the MMSI is in your name table. Tune an inland channel (156.3 to 162.0 MHz; 10 and 6 are common intership channels)

DGPS differential beacons, 283.5 - 325 kHz: MSK at 50, 100 or 200 bit/s (found by itself) carrying RTCM SC-104 messages: the station ID, carrier offset, level, every message with its parity checked, and the decoded content (satellite corrections, reference station position, beacon almanac, station text; receive only)

GK-2A (GEO-KOMPSAT-2A, Korea, 128.2°E) LRIT on 1692.14 MHz: BPSK at 128 ksym/s, rate 1/2 Viterbi, Reed-Solomon (255,223), CCSDS frames, xRIT files with full-disk pictures per channel (JPEG 2000, put together from their segments), schedule and additional-data text. KMA encrypts the pictures with DES: import your KMA key file to see them (none are built in); the .lrit files are saved either way. Needs a dish with an LNA and GK-2A above your horizon (East Asia, Australia, western Pacific). Receive only

GK-2A (GEO-KOMPSAT-2A, Korea, 128.2°E) HRIT on 1695.4 MHz: QPSK at 3 Msym/s (3 Mbit/s of frames), rate 1/2 Viterbi, Reed-Solomon (255,223), CCSDS frames, xRIT files with the 16-channel full-disk pictures (JPEG 2000, assembled from their segments). KMA encrypts the pictures with DES: import your KMA key file to see them (none are built in); the .lrit files are saved either way. Needs a dish with an LNA, a radio that runs 6.4 Msps or more and GK-2A above your horizon. Receive only

FengYun-4 LRIT on 1697 MHz, FY-4A (104.7°E, DVB-S2 QPSK 2/5 at 90 ksym/s) or FY-4B (DVB-S2 QPSK 8/9 at 120 ksym/s; the satellite is a choice in the panel), carrying CCSDS xRIT files. The AGRI pictures (JPEG 2000 segments, put together per channel and region), text and admin files, with the DVB-S2 lock, the data units and a hint when nothing decodes. Needs a dish (about 1 m) with an LNA and filter at the feed. Receive only

FengYun-4A HRIT-II/III on 1679 MHz: DVB-S2 QPSK 5/6 at 1 Msym/s carrying CCSDS xRIT files, the full-resolution AGRI pictures per channel and region (JPEG 2000). Needs a dish (about 1.2 m or more) with an LNA and filter. Receive only

FengYun-2 (FY-2G 105°E, FY-2H 79°E) S-VISSR on 1687.5 MHz: uncoded differential BPSK at 660 ksym/s, one scan line per frame. Pictures of IR1 10.8, IR2 12, IR3 6.75 (water vapour), IR4 3.75 um and the visible channel (half resolution), built line by line over about 25 minutes; the bit error ratio comes from the known preamble. Needs a dish (about 1.2 m) with an LNA and filter. Receive only

COSPAS-SARSAT 406 MHz distress beacons (EPIRB, ELT, PLB) on 406.025 - 406.076 MHz: 400 bit/s Manchester phase modulation, a burst of half a second about every 50 seconds. The 15 hex ID, the protocol, the country, the identification (MMSI, serial, aircraft address) and the position when the beacon sends one, both BCH checks, the 121.5 MHz homing flag, and a map. Receive only

Argos satellite data collection, receive only. Uplink on 401.650 MHz (401.618 - 401.680): PTT-A2 bursts (160 ms carrier, then 400 bit/s Manchester phase modulation of +-1.1 rad) decoded to the 28 bit platform ID and the user data in hex, with each platform\'s burst frequencies as its Doppler and drift curve; PTT-A3, ZE and Argos-4 bursts are only counted and timed (their specifications are not public). Downlink on 465.9875 MHz from MetOp-B / -C: the carrier followed through the pass Doppler and compared with the predicted curve, 400 bit/s Manchester bits and HDLC frames in hex with their FCS (the frame contents are not public)
UAT on 978 MHz: ADS-B position and identity reports, FIS-B weather text products and TIS-B traffic relay (DO-282). Typical 1 Msps capture. Receive only

FY-3 AHRPT, the Fengyun-3 polar weather satellites (QPSK, two convolutional codes, 1701.4 MHz at 2.6 Msym/s for FY-3C and 1704.5 MHz at 2.8 Msym/s for FY-3A / B; FY-3D to FY-3H send it in X-band): VIRR and MERSI pictures line by line, the symbol rate measured by itself. Needs a dish (about 1 m or more, tracking the satellite) with an LNA at the feed and a fast radio (4 Msps or more: HackRF, Airspy, SDRplay, Pluto; not an RTL-SDR)

FY-3 MPT, the medium rate picture transmission of FY-3A, FY-3B and FY-3C (X-band 7750 / 7780 MHz, QPSK 18.7 Msym/s): the MERSI pictures, 250 m channels on the 1 km grid. Needs a dish with an X-band feed, a down-converter and a radio that samples 28 Msps or more (20 Msps gives a reduced result)

PACTOR-II, receive only, physical layer: the two D-PSK carriers 200 Hz apart at 100 baud are found by their symbol clock, the phase steps are recovered and shown, and the frame period and the constant part of a repeating frame are measured. The channel coding (convolutional code, interleaver, scrambler) is proprietary (SCS) and not published, so no text is produced

PACTOR-III, receive only, physical layer: 2 to 18 D-PSK carriers on the 120 Hz grid 480 + 120 n Hz at 100 baud, the carrier set (speed level) and the repeating frame structure. The channel coding is proprietary (SCS) and not published, so no text is produced

PACTOR-IV, receive only, physical layer: the single PSK carrier at 1500 Hz with 1800 baud (speed levels 5 to 10) is found by its symbol clock and its constellation is estimated. The chirp and spread-spectrum levels 1 to 4, the equaliser, the channel coding and the frame format are not available, so no text is produced

Finds out which digital voice system is on the air (DMR, P25 phase 1 / 2, NXDN, D-STAR, dPMR, Yaesu Fusion, TETRA, M17, or analogue FM) from its frame syncs, lists every one in the captured span and switches to the decoder

APCO Project 25 Phase 2 (TIA-102.BBAB) TDMA, two time slots, 6000 symbols/s differential QPSK in 12.5 kHz: talkgroups, unit IDs, voice grants and the trunking system. The frame layout is a first reading of public descriptions and has not been tried on a real signal (receive only; encrypted calls are only reported)

Signalling tones on narrow-FM audio or sound-card audio: CTCSS sub-audible tones (50 tones with the measured frequency), DCS codes (23 bit Golay word, normal and inverted, with the 83-code list), DTMF keys, five-tone sequential calls (ZVEI1, ZVEI2, CCIR, EEA, EIA, DZVEI), aviation SELCAL pairs and a generic two-tone paging detector, with a live tone and spectrum display, a history of everything heard and a squelch-style gate that opens the audio only for a chosen CTCSS tone or DCS code. Receive only

MPT 1327 analog trunking control channels (UK MPT 1327 / MPT 1343, VHF and UHF): 1200 bit/s FFSK on the FM control channel: lock, the codewords received good and bad, the system identity, a list of the control messages (time, type, caller and called address, channel number) and the channel table. Control channel only: no traffic channel audio is decoded and nothing encrypted is decoded (receive only)

LTR (Logic Trunked Radio) control data: the 300 bit/s subaudible words on a repeater channel (area, go-to, home, ID, free repeater). Control data only, no voice; every word is accepted only when its 7 check bits verify (receive only)

EDACS control channel, 9600 bit/s GFSK: the outbound frames framed by the dotting, three copies voted, the 12 BCH check bits verified, the Barker sync word, and the calls, talkgroups and site read in the Standard / Networked layout (or Extended Addressing), a power scan of the voice channels of a frequency table you enter, and following of an analog voice channel in a wide capture. No ProVoice (digital voice) decoding, nothing encrypted (receive only)

Sensors on 433.92 MHz (also 315, 868 and 915 MHz) with the decoders of rtl_433: weather stations, thermometers, tyre pressure, door and smoke sensors, meters, remotes. OOK / ASK and FSK pulse slicer, a live list with history graphs, CSV / JSON / MQTT-style export, and an analyser that shows the pulses and bits of a signal nobody decodes and saves a custom (flex) decoder for it. Which sensors are supported is listed in docs/SENSORS-3.7.md; not every sensor on the air is covered

Sferics: the radio crackles of lightning discharges below about 30 MHz, strongest at VLF / LF. Counts strikes and flashes, strikes per minute, a 60 minute activity histogram and the time, strength and width of every strike on the sample clock; a regular 100 / 120 Hz impulse train (mains interference) is recognised and left out. One receiver gives when and how strong, not where: a position needs the arrival times of several stations (a network such as Blitzortung). Receive only

BLE tracker detector (2402 / 2426 / 2480 MHz): recognises Apple Find My accessories such as AirTag, Tile, Chipolo, Samsung SmartTag and Google Find My Device tags from their advertisements, shows how long and how close each stays and warns about one that follows you (receive only; identifiers are kept for a short window and never saved)

Thread (the IPv6 mesh of Matter smart homes) on the 2.4 GHz 802.15.4 channels 11 - 26 (O-QPSK, 250 kbit/s): networks from their beacons (network name, extended PAN ID, version), devices from their 802.15.4 addresses, 6LoWPAN headers (mesh, fragments, IPHC, UDP ports, MLE and CoAP) where a frame is sent in the clear, a live frame log; channel scan. Receive only. Almost all Thread traffic is AES-CCM encrypted at the link layer: those frames show the 802.15.4 header, the frame counter and key index and are marked encrypted; their content (IPv6, MLE, CoAP) is not readable without the network key, and OnAir does not decrypt or recover keys. Needs a fast radio (4 Msps or more), not an RTL-SDR

Wi-SUN FAN smart utility networks (smart meters, street lights) (IEEE 802.15.4g FSK at 50, 100 and 150 kbit/s) with the band plans of every Wi-SUN region from 470 MHz to 2.4 GHz: a whole band at once (the nodes hop over every channel, all of 915 - 928 MHz at 16 Msps), networks with their name and border router, nodes with vendor, role, routing cost and schedules, links with the levels acks report, a frame log and a hop chart. Receive only: nothing is sent or joined; PAN configurations and data are encrypted and stay so. Needs 16 Msps or more for the whole band (a few channels from 2 Msps)

Wireless M-Bus (EN 13757-4) utility meters: S1 on 868.3 MHz, T1 and C1 on 868.95 MHz, R2 on 868.03 - 868.15 MHz and N1 on 169.4 MHz, with Wize frames (169 MHz, 2.4 / 4.8 kbit/s, format B, CI 0x20: network, application, counter and time stamp; the L7 data stays encrypted) (2-FSK / GFSK, Manchester, 3-out-of-6 and NRZ chips, frame formats A and B with their block CRCs): manufacturer, meter ID, version and device type (water, heat, gas, electricity, heat cost allocator), and for unencrypted frames the readings (volume, energy, power, temperatures, dates). Encrypted payloads are listed as encrypted and never decoded. Needs a radio with 1 Msps or more

NFC / RFID at 13.56 MHz, receive only: ISO/IEC 14443 Type A (REQA/WUPA, ATQA, anticollision, SELECT, SAK, UID sizes, CRC_A, HLTA, RATS/ATS, APDU framing as hex, NDEF text/URI from Type 2 READ answers), Type B (REQB/ATQB on the BPSK subcarrier) and ISO/IEC 15693 (1-of-4 / 1-of-256 pulse position, inventory, UID, system info) as far as the public specs allow. Reader frames are 100%% ASK Miller; tag answers load-modulate the 847.5 kHz (14443) or 423.75 kHz (15693) subcarrier. Needs an HF-capable receiver (RTL-SDR V4 direct HF, HackRF, Airspy HF+, RX888) at a few Msps so the +-847.5 kHz sidebands fit. Nothing is cloned, no encrypted content is decoded, no keys are attacked. Pet microchips are 134.2 kHz FDX-B, a different band (see docs/NFC.md)

Z-Wave home automation (ITU-T G.9959 FSK: R1 9.6 kbit/s Manchester, R2 40 kbit/s, R3 100 kbit/s) on the sub-GHz channels of Europe, USA, Australia / New Zealand, Hong Kong, India, Russia, China, Israel, Japan and Korea: networks by home ID, nodes, command classes and commands, a frame log. Receive only: S0 and S2 encrypted payloads are shown as encrypted and never decoded. Europe fits in 2 Msps centred on 869.13 MHz

Sigfox uplinks, receive only: ultra-narrowband D-BPSK at 100 bit/s (RC1 868.130 MHz, RC3, RC5, RC6) or 600 bit/s (RC2 902.200 MHz, RC4) anywhere in the 200 kHz macro channel. Each frame\'s type, device ID, message counter, payload in hex (or the single bit), the downlink request flag and the authentication code (shown, never checked: it needs the device key), the CRC checked, and the three repetitions (ranks 1 - 3, each with its own convolution code) merged into one message with their frequencies and level. Frame layout from the public Sigfox radio specification. Nothing is decrypted

e-Czas, the Polish national time service (GUM) on the 225 kHz long-wave carrier of Polish Radio 1: 50 bit/s phase keying, time packets with the date, the local offset, the summer-time and leap-second flags and the transmitter state, and how far the computer clock is off. Needs a radio that tunes to 225 kHz (or an upconverter)

Meteor scatter detector: forward-scatter echoes of a fixed beacon (the GRAVES space radar at 143.050 MHz, or any CW beacon) found in a narrow spectrogram next to its line. Each ping is counted with its start time, duration, peak level over the background and Doppler shift; ping rate per hour and per day with the annual meteor showers marked, a live echo waterfall, CSV logging for unattended runs. Needs a radio that tunes to the beacon (2 Msps or more; the beacon within 4 kHz of the centre)

GOES / Meteosat data collection platforms (DCS) on the 401.7 - 402.1 MHz uplink: river gauges, weather stations, tide gauges and buoys send a short report on their own 1.5 kHz channel at 100, 300 or 1200 bps (carrier phase modulation, NRZ or Manchester). Every carrier in the capture is followed and every bit rate and coding is tried; the BCH-protected 8-hex-digit platform address, the satellite channel, the level and the ASCII or pseudo-binary sensor data are shown, with a table of the platforms heard and a CSV log. Needs a radio that covers 401.7 - 402.1 MHz (0.5 Msps or more) and a UHF antenna

SBAS L1 augmentation satellites (WAAS, EGNOS, MSAS, GAGAN, SDCM, BDSBAS) on 1575.42 MHz: found and tracked without a GPS lock first, every message decoded with its CRC (PRN mask, fast corrections and UDRE, ionospheric grid, GEO navigation message, time offset, almanac). Receive only: the corrections are shown, not applied. Needs an active antenna
JT4 EME weak-signal contacts (4-FSK, convolutional code, 47 s transmissions, sub-modes A to G)
MT63 keyboard chat (500 / 1000 / 2000 Hz, short or long interleave, found automatically): 64 carriers with Walsh-Hadamard coded characters that survive fades and interference, 14.1095 MHz
FSQ (Fast Simple QSO) keyboard chat: 33 tones, speeds 1.5 to 6 baud found automatically, directed messages with sender, addressee and command, 14.105 MHz
IFKP (Incremental Frequency Keying Plus) keyboard chat: 33 tones, speeds 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 found automatically, 14.083 MHz

SITOR-B (FEC) teletype, CCIR 476 / ITU-R M.476, 100 baud FSK with 170 Hz shift: NAVTEX on 518 / 490 kHz and HF coast stations. The FSK tones, the polarity and the character phase are found automatically and the text is shown as it is received. SITOR-A / AMTOR (ARQ) links are monitored too: both stations, the selective call, repeats dropped by following the control signals, changes of direction (SITOR-A tested on simulated signals). Receive only

DME (distance measuring equipment) on 962-1213 MHz: the channel (number from the tuned frequency, X or Y from the pulse spacing: 12 us, 30 us reply, 36 us interrogation) of the beacon from its pulse pairs, the pair rate and the Morse ident, found as a regular 1350 pairs per second train; on a TACAN beacon also the radial, from the 15 and 135 Hz modulation and the reference bursts; receive only (the slant range needs an interrogation, which OnAir does not send), needs a radio that tunes to about 1 GHz at 2 Msps or more

Loran-C at 100 kHz: the group repetition interval, the master and secondary stations with their arrival times relative to the master, level and phase code, and the chain that uses the GRI (Loran-C chains and the Russian Chayka chains, which send the same 100 kHz pulse groups). The eLoran data channel (9th pulse, Eurofix) is not decoded: the Reed-Solomon constants and message layouts of the Loran Data Channel standard are not public text. Receive only, needs a radio or downconverter that tunes to 100 kHz at 250 ksps or more

ASTERIX surveillance data from a network or a file (no radio): CAT 021 ADS-B target reports, CAT 048 monoradar target reports and CAT 062 system tracks as UDP datagrams (unicast or multicast) or a recording (raw blocks or a pcap capture), shown as a track table and a map. A radar\'s own pulses cannot be received by a software radio; this reads the data a radar or ground station sends. Receive only, the port is closed until you start listening

ARDOP (Amateur Radio Digital Open Protocol, the HF modem of Winlink) frames on 200, 500, 1000 and 2000 Hz channels, monitor only: the two-tone leader and the 4FSK frame type of every frame, connect requests, IDs and pings with call signs and grid square, ACK / NAK quality, and the data of the 4FSK frames that pass their CRC; PSK and QAM data frames are listed by header

Yaesu System Fusion (C4FM 4800 symbols/s, 12.5 kHz), 2 m and 70 cm. Receive only: callsigns, call mode and slow data are decoded (the frames are bit-identical to what MMDVMHost writes); V/D mode 1 voice plays through the mbelib you install for DMR and NXDN, the other voice types need a speech codec plug-in that you install yourself

Shortwave: the general receiver (AM, USB, LSB, CW) with a strip of one-click HF decoders: tune to a signal, press RTTY, CW, PSK31, FT8, SSTV, Olivia, ALE, NAVTEX ... and the text appears below the waterfall, without leaving the window or the frequency

LoRaWAN across a whole regional plan at once: every channel of EU868, US915, AU915, AS923-1..4 or EU433 that fits the captured band (125 / 250 / 500 kHz, SF7 - SF12, gateway downlinks on inverted IQ) and the FSK channel (DR7, 50 kbit/s GFSK on 868.8 MHz in EU868), shown in one table with time, channel, SF, DevAddr, frame counter, port, MIC, MAC commands, join request / accept framing, level and SNR. Receive only and keyless: payloads are encrypted with the devices\' session keys and stay bytes; no key is handled and nothing is decrypted

LoRa from satellites and space gateway services on 400 - 440 MHz and 868 / 915 MHz: the LoRa decoder with a Doppler-wide channel filter that follows the carrier through every frame (shift of up to +-10 kHz at 436 MHz and +-20 kHz at 868 MHz, rate of up to 150 - 300 Hz/s), a Doppler curve of the pass drawn from the frames, public presets (unverified) and the pass planner naming the satellite. Receive only

General BPSK / QPSK / OQPSK / 8PSK demodulator and analyser for satellite and other PSK signals: finds the signal nearest the dial, measures its symbol rate (any rate the radio holds, from about 50 Bd), order, pulse shape, carrier, Doppler and Eb/N0 by itself, then demodulates it with a constellation and eye diagram, follows the Doppler of a pass, decodes differential coding and the G3RUH / CCSDS scramblers, finds a sync word and saves the bits. Receive only; experimental (checked against generated signals only)

HF military / government waveform identifier (identification only): measures the band, baud rate, tone spacing, constellation order, repetition period and pilot tones of an HF signal and ranks candidate waveforms (STANAG 4285, MIL-STD-188-110, Link 11, ALE, MFSK families, the Buzzer). Estimates only: nothing is decoded, no message content is read, no encryption is touched

PACTOR-I monitor, receive only and experimental (no real recording was available): 100 and 200 baud FSK with 200 Hz shift found automatically (tone pair, speed, shift polarity and timing), the 1.25 s ARQ cycle of both stations of a link, packets checked with their CRC-16, connect packets with the called callsign, control signals CS1 - CS4, changeovers and QRT, plain ASCII and Huffman text, repeats and unproto / FEC broadcasts, memory ARQ (bad copies are added up). PACTOR-II, -III and -IV have their own modes (physical layer only: their coding is proprietary and not decoded)

ROS weak-signal HF chat mode (detector, text decoding partial): the sideband audio goes to a waterfall, and every 2 s the last 16 s are measured for the publicly described ROS physical layer, one tone at a time on a fine grid (about 144 tones, 15.6 Hz apart), about 2.25 kHz wide, 4 / 8 / 16 baud. A detection names the sub-mode (ROS 4 / 8 / 16 baud), the tone range and the grid, and marks the band on the waterfall. The text is NOT decoded: the framing, coding and FEC of ROS are not published (partial, needs a public spec); use the ROS program to read it

SSDV (Slow Scan Digital Video) pictures from high-altitude balloons and amateur satellites: FM / FSK channel, 256-byte SSDV packets checked with their CRC-32 and the Reed-Solomon code, the JPEG rebuilt as packets arrive (grey where packets are missing), saved as JPEG when complete. Plain FSK 1200 - 19200 baud and RTTY-framed bytes 300 - 1200 baud are tried at the same time, both polarities. Wenet, the Project Horus high-speed link (2-FSK 115.2 kbaud with LDPC, or the 96 kbaud sound-card version), is received at the same time when the sample rate is 2 MHz or more (needs a user test with a real recording). Scrambled / AX.25 / IL2P framing and LoRa are not handled. SSDV code by Philip Heron (GPL-3.0-or-later); Wenet code tables by Project Horus (GPL-3.0-or-later)

Railway balise up-link, receive only and untested on air (no real recording was available): the Eurobalise FSK up-link around 4.234 MHz (3.951 / 4.516 MHz, 564.48 kbit/s) decoded to the long (1023 bit) and short (341 bit) telegrams of UNISIG SUBSET-036 with the header fields NID_C, NID_BG, N_PIG. The train\'s tele-powering field is 27.095 MHz AM and is not received. EBICab 700 (32 bit) and 900 (255 bit) telegram formats are not published: such bursts are listed with their length and first bits only. Needs a radio that reaches 4.2 MHz at 4 Msps or more

Every Inmarsat L-band carrier in one wide capture, decoded at the same time: Aero P channels (600, 1200 and 10500 bit/s, ACARS and ADS-C with an aircraft map) and Inmarsat-C (EGC safety and news broadcasts), found and listed automatically with a CPU budget. Aero C voice channels are demodulated and decoded (framing from JAERO, checked on a recorded call); sound needs the AMBE plug-in you build yourself (never shipped). Best with a radio that does 6 Msps or more (Airspy, SDRplay, HackRF); an RTL-SDR at 2.4 Msps covers one P group. Synthetic signals only so far: needs a user test with a real capture

nRF24L01 / nRF24L01+ Enhanced ShockBurst sniffer, receive only and untested on air (no real recording was available): 2.4 GHz channel N = 2400 + N MHz (N = 0..125), GFSK at 250 kbit/s, 1 and 2 Mbit/s tried together, frames with a 3 to 5 byte address, 9-bit control field (length, PID, NO_ACK), up to 32 payload bytes and CRC-8 or CRC-16. The address is found by trying the candidate positions and lengths and accepting a valid CRC; a CRC-8 frame is shown when seen three times. Needs a 2.4 GHz SDR: HackRF One / Pro, PlutoSDR (extended range), bladeRF, LimeSDR, USRP B200 / B210; RTL-SDR, Airspy R2 / Mini and SDRplay do not reach 2.4 GHz

Chat with Flipper Zero devices running the Enhanced Sub-GHz Chat app (or the firmware\'s CLI Sub-GHz chat), receive and send: CC1101 GFSK at 9.99 kbaud with 19 kHz deviation on 433.92 MHz or any frequency the Flippers use. Heard lines appear in a chat with level and frequency offset; lines are sent through a transmit-capable radio (HackRF and others). Plain chats, or encrypted ones with the same password or hex key as the Flippers (AES-256-GCM with replay protection, as the app does). On a half-duplex radio the receiver pauses while a line is sent. Transmitting needs the right to use the frequency where you are
Mode Builder: describe a digital protocol (modulation, sync word, frame, FEC, CRC, fields) and decode it without code; your custom modes are listed here
Plugins: add decoders and actions without rebuilding OnAir; installed plugins, their permissions and logs

KAAL: a 10 kHz wide digital voice and station-identity link (16 kbit/s voice codec, 16-QAM with LDPC, a sweep signature and a beacon side channel). Receive plays the speech and shows the last beacon (callsign, grid, position, power, text); transmit takes a microphone or a WAV file, to a radio or an IQ file

KAVB: the video mode of the KAAL family, 1 to 2 MHz wide (700 to 1400 ksym/s single carrier, 16-QAM and 64-QAM with LDPC, a sweep signature, video, audio and data packets in FEC groups). Receive finds the frames and lists the packets with the link numbers and a constellation, counts the payload bytes and can save them to a file; there is no AV1 or Opus decoder in this build, so no picture or sound is shown. Transmit sends a file of bytes or a synthetic test stream, to a radio or an IQ file

KAIT: a 1080p picture in a 10 s burst, 190 kHz wide, coded in layers (a coarse picture first in the most robust coding, then more detail): the picture a receiver shows is what its link decodes, from an outline at -12 dB to the full picture above 8 dB. Receive shows the picture growing layer by layer with the callsign and the link numbers; transmit takes a PNG or PPM picture (or a demo picture), to a radio or an IQ file

KAPP: the packet mode of the KAAL family, 100 kHz wide (80 ksym/s, BPSK to 1024-QAM with LDPC, bursts with selective repeat). Receive lists the messages that arrive whole with the profile, SNR, counts and a constellation; it only listens and sends no acknowledgement. Transmit sends a text or a file one-way, repeated, to a radio or an IQ file

KAFT: the file transfer mode of the KAAL family, 200 kHz, 500 kHz or 1 MHz wide (ten profiles from BPSK 1/4 to 1024-QAM 9/10, LDPC blocks with CRC-32, a hash check of the whole file). Receive follows the transfer and saves each verified file to a folder you choose; it only listens and sends no reply. Transmit sends a file one-way, repeated, to a radio or an IQ file

KAWS: the HF weak-signal chat and beacon mode of the KAAL family, 2.4 kHz wide (eight profiles from chirp spread spectrum for the weakest signals to OFDM, LDPC blocks with CRC-16, a woven-lattice preamble, 15 s to 120 s UTC slots). Receive lists the chat messages and beacons that arrive, with the profile, SNR estimate and the preamble indicator, from upper-sideband audio; it only listens and sends no acknowledgement. Transmit sends a chat message or a beacon one-way, repeated, to a radio or an IQ file. The slots come from the computer clock, which must be UTC-accurate. KAWS is simulation-only: it has never been on the air, and the voice profiles need a speech codec that you install

NOAA APT analogue pictures on 137 MHz: FM, the 2400 Hz subcarrier, sync A, two channels side by side growing line by line and saved as PNG. NOAA-15, -18 and -19 stopped transmitting in 2025, so this mode is for recordings; pick a recording with File > Open

NOAA HRPT on 1698 / 1702.5 / 1707 MHz: PM with a residual carrier, Manchester 665.4 kbit/s, 11090-word minor frames, the AVHRR picture and HIRS from the TIP. NOAA-15, -18 and -19 stopped transmitting in 2025, so this mode is for recordings

NOAA GAC on-board recorder dump: BPSK 2.6616 Msym/s, scrambled 3327-word frames, the reduced AVHRR picture (409 pixels) and HIRS. NOAA-15, -18 and -19 stopped transmitting in 2025, so this mode is for recordings
NOAA DSB on 137.35 / 137.77 MHz: PM, Manchester 8320 bit/s, 104-byte TIP minor frames, spacecraft ID, HIRS picture. NOAA-15, -18 and -19 stopped transmitting in 2025, so this mode is for recordings

Meteor-M HRPT on 1700 MHz: PM with a residual carrier, Manchester 665.4 kbit/s, 1024-byte CADUs, the MSU-MR picture line by line (6 channels, a colour composite). Needs a dish at 1.7 GHz and 3 Msps or more; Follow the next pass tunes with Doppler and starts by itself

Elektro-L RDAS downlink, X-band 7500 MHz: BPSK 30.72 Msym/s, NRZ-M, CADUs, the MSU-GS infrared disc (7 channels, 3294 x 3400) and a reduced visible picture. Needs an X-band dish and 40 Msps or more; recordings work
Arktika-M RDAS, X-band 7865 MHz: the same MSU-GS downlink as Elektro-L RDAS, from a highly elliptical orbit. Needs an X-band dish, 40 Msps or more and Doppler tracking; recordings work

Arktika-M N1 / N2 space-weather telemetry (GGAK, experimental: frame lock not reached yet) on 1703 MHz, PM 5 ksym/s: the Elektro GGAK frames and magnetometer. Highly elliptical orbit: Follow the next pass tracks the Doppler

Arctic Weather Satellite on 1707 MHz: QPSK 1.785 Msym/s, CCSDS convolutional code, Reed-Solomon interleave 5, the MWR microwave scans (19 channels, 145 points) line by line. Needs a dish at 1.7 GHz and 4 Msps or more; Follow the next pass tunes with Doppler and starts by itself

Inmarsat BGAN (ETSI TS 102 744 Family SL), the satellite data service: every forward carrier from 1525 to 1559 MHz, bearer type and code rate, satellite, spot beam, network identity, and the system information it broadcasts. One-click scan across the band. Signalling and carrier structure only: no voice, no user data, no subscriber identity. Needs a user test: only synthetic signals so far, never validated on a real BGAN recording. A patch antenna is enough for the global beam and for bearers aimed at your region; narrow spot beams elsewhere are out of reach

ADS-L (EASA ADS-L 4 SRD-860): the iConspicuity broadcast of light aircraft, gliders, paragliders and drones on 868.2, 868.4 and 869.525 MHz. Traffic, status and ground uplink packets give position, altitude, speed, category and address on the map and in a table. Tuned to 868.875 MHz at 2 Msps one capture holds every channel and also FLARM. Receive only; no key is needed

Meteosat Second Generation raw downlink on 1686.83 MHz: QPSK 3.75 Msym/s, CCSDS convolutional code, Reed-Solomon interleave 5, the SEVIRI disc line by line (11 channels and HRV, reduced to fit memory, saved when the disc ends every 15 minutes). Needs a fixed dish of about 1.2 m or more at 1.7 GHz with an LNA and 6 Msps. Receive only

HimawariCast file broadcast from JCSAT-2B, C-band 4148 MHz (1002 MHz after a 5150 MHz LNB): DVB-S2 QPSK 2/3 at 2.586 Msym/s, IP over MPE on PID 1001, Fazzt files. The Himawari full discs put together from their ten HRIT segments per channel and saved as PNG, and every other file saved as it comes. Needs a C-band dish of about 1.8 m or more, an LNB and 4.5 Msps. Receive only

GeoNetCast Americas file broadcast, C-band 4080 MHz (1070 MHz after a 5150 MHz LNB): DVB-S2 8PSK 5/6 at 30 Msym/s, IP over MPE on PID 4201, Fazzt files, saved as they come (satellite pictures and weather products in their own formats). Needs a C-band dish and 52 Msps or more, so most radios can only play a recording. Receive only
Reticulum mesh traffic on RNode LoRa: announces with their signature checked, packet types and destinations; data stays encrypted, structure only

ExpressLRS RC links on the 900 MHz LoRa rates: link id, rate and hop index from SYNC frames; RC channels only with your own binding phrase (Advanced). 2.4 GHz FLRC and long-interleaver LoRa are not decodable
MAVLink telemetry on SiK / 3DR radios at 433 and 915 MHz: GFSK frequency hopping, every air speed, MAVLink v1 / v2 messages with vehicle position on the map
FrSky D8 and D16 2.4 GHz RC links (CC2500 GFSK, hopping): transmitter id and channels; layouts from the DIY-Multiprotocol-TX-Module project, simulated signals only so far
FlySky AFHDS and AFHDS 2A 2.4 GHz RC links (A7105 GFSK, hopping): transmitter id and channels; layouts from the DIY-Multiprotocol-TX-Module project, simulated signals only so far

Motorola Type II trunking (SmartNet, SmartZone): 3600 bit/s control channel, talkgroups, sites, calls followed inside the capture (analog as FM, digital through the P25 receiver and the user-installed IMBE plug-in)
TETRA Direct Mode (terminal to terminal, or through a DM repeater or gateway): the addresses, the calls and clear speech (with the user-installed TETRA codec); encrypted calls are listed, not decoded
OpenSky (M/A-COM / Harris) identifier: measures the symbol rate, the levels, the width and the TDMA burst pattern; the air interface is not public and the traffic is encrypted, so nothing is decoded

Bluetooth Classic (BR/EDR) discovery over a wide capture of the 2.4 GHz band: every packet starts with the sync word of its piconet master\'s LAP, so devices and piconets in use are listed by LAP; a discoverable device that answers an inquiry also gives its full address and class of device. The radio hops over 79 channels of 1 MHz, so a HackRF at 20 Msps hears about a quarter of the packets. Receive only: never inquires, pages or answers; payloads are not decoded

CB radio, 27 MHz: the 40-channel plan of your region (CEPT, the German 80, the UK 27/81 or the USA), AM, FM and SSB decided from the signal, every channel of the span at once, a busy-channel list and a scan
FRS and GMRS (USA, Canada) 462 and 467 MHz, 22 channels, narrow FM with the CTCSS tone or DCS code of each transmission, GMRS repeater outputs, a busy-channel list and a scan
Analog PMR446 (Europe) 446.00625 - 446.19375 MHz, 16 channels, narrow FM with the CTCSS tone or DCS code of each transmission, a busy-channel list and a scan
MDC-1200 (Motorola) unit ID bursts on analog FM: every FM carrier of the span is followed and the 1200 bit/s burst that opens or closes a transmission is decoded. FleetSync is not decoded

Finds wireless microphones and in-ear monitors: wide FM carriers in the UHF bands of your region (470 - 694 MHz, 823 - 832 MHz, 863 - 865 MHz; USA 470 - 698, 902 - 928, 944 - 952 MHz), with width, deviation and FM or not, and a click to listen

Amateur FM repeaters and simplex on 2 m and 70 cm: the repeater outputs of your IARU region with their input offsets, the CTCSS tone or DCS code heard on each, calling channels, a busy-channel list and a scan

HF voice in USB on fixed frequencies: the HFGCS primary frequencies (4724, 8992, 11175 and 15016 kHz), the MARS and Canadian Forces relays and the VOLMET weather broadcasts with their schedules; the scan retunes the radio and stays on one that is on the air

FANET (Skytraxx open protocol, LoRa SF7 at 868.2 MHz in Europe, 920.8 MHz elsewhere): paragliders and hang gliders. Tracking, ground status, names, messages and weather stations in a table and on a map. Receive only.

OGN tracker radio protocol on 868.2 and 868.4 MHz, 100 kchip/s Manchester FSK with LDPC, the FLARM air format with its own sync word. Gliders and light aircraft, position, altitude and speed in a table and on a map. Positions marked encrypted are counted and not read. Receive only.

GBAS VHF data broadcast (108 - 118 MHz) for satellite landing systems. Bursts in 62.5 ms slots and the 10 500 symbol/s line are detected. The message content is not read: the burst format is only in documents that are not public.
LDACS L-band digital aeronautical link, 625 kHz OFDM: detected by its cyclic prefix (symbol period, prefix, carrier offset). Structure only, nothing is decoded.
AeroMACS airport data link, 5091 - 5150 MHz, 5 MHz WiMAX-profile OFDM: detected by its cyclic prefix and 5 ms frames. Structure only, nothing is decoded. Needs at least 5.6 Msps.

US end-of-train telemetry on 457.9375 MHz and head-of-train commands on 452.9375 MHz: 1200 bit/s AFSK on FM, the AAR frame with its BCH check. Unit number, brake pipe pressure, motion and battery from the end of the train (tested on a real recording). Head-of-train frames are shown only when they use the same frame check; their fields are not decoded. Receive only.
5.8 GHz tolling, EN 12253 downlink at 500 kbit/s: frames and their class are counted. Identifying structure only: link identifiers and any content are not shown or saved.
Vehicle safety messages on 5.9 GHz, 802.11p 10 MHz channels at 3 and 6 Mbit/s: BSM (SAE J2735) and CAM (ETSI) positions in a table and on a map. Needs at least 10 Msps. Receive only.
LTE sidelink vehicle links on 5.9 GHz (10 MHz): detected by the 1 ms subframe and SC-FDMA cyclic prefix. Structure only: the safety messages are not decoded. Needs at least 15.36 Msps.
ERMES (ETS 300 133) pan-European paging, 169.4 - 169.8 MHz, 4-level FM at 6250 bit/s: network identity, addresses, and numeric or text messages. Tune one 25 kHz channel. Receive only.

Pulse radar detection (S or X band with a suitable receiver): rotation rate, pulse repetition frequency, pulse width and beamwidth from the beam passing. A bearing needs direction finding with two coherent channels. FMCW radars are not seen.
Weather radar detection (C or S band): rotation, single or dual pulse repetition frequency, pulse width and the elevation sweeps of the scan pattern.
GOES-R series GRB on 1686.6 MHz: DVB-S2, 8.67 Msym/s, CADUs with ABI pictures (JPEG 2000), SUVI, GLM and metadata. Needs an L-band dish and 12 Msps or more
GOES GVAR, the 2.11 Msym/s BPSK imager broadcast of the GOES-13 to 15 generation on 1685.7 MHz: the imager visible and infrared lines. GOES-N is retired, so this mode opens recordings
GOES CDA telemetry downlink on 1693 / 1694 MHz: GOES-R (40 or 4 kbit/s, BPSK with CCSDS frames) or GOES-N (PM, 4 kbit/s): frame log and virtual channels
GOES-N MDL (multi-use data link) on 1681.5 MHz: QPSK 200 ksym/s, 464-byte frames in a frame log
GK-2A UHRIT on 8070 MHz: DVB-S2, 15.6 Msym/s, CADUs with xRIT files. Needs an X-band dish, a down-converter and about 28 Msps or more; recordings work
GK-2A CDAS service: QPSK 3.096 Msym/s, CCSDS frames with Reed-Solomon, frame log and virtual channels. Needs a dish and 8 Msps

S-band and L-band CCSDS downlinks: pick the satellite from the table (Jason-3, CloudSat, FORMOSAT, Hinode, SMAP, Falcon 9, Starship, Crew Dragon and many others), tuning and frame format are set for you. Frames, virtual channels and spacecraft IDs; Needs a tracking S-band dish
Geoscan cubesats on 70 cm (StratoSat-TK1, RTU-MIREA1, TUSUR-GO, VIZARD-ION, COLIBRI-S, HORIZON): 9600 bit/s FSK, 66-byte frames with CRC. A 70 cm Yagi or vertical works during a pass
Lucky-7 cubesat on 437.525 MHz: 4800 bit/s FSK, 35-byte frames with telemetry and picture chunks
AMSAT-F Spino cubesat on 435.2 MHz: 2400 bit/s FSK, variable-length frames with CRC
ERMINAZ cubesat on 435.775 MHz: 9600 bit/s FSK, CCSDS frames with Reed-Solomon

MIL-STD-188-110A/C fixed-frequency serial tone modem, receive only: 2400 Bd 8-PSK on 1800 Hz, 75 to 4800 bit/s. The preamble gives speed and interleaver, then probes, deinterleaver and Viterbi decoding, with STANAG 5066 D_PDU framing when present. Tested on simulated signals.

STANAG 4285 HF modem, receive only: 2400 Bd frames of 256 symbols, 75 to 3600 bit/s. Coded speeds found automatically from the code and its start pattern; uncoded speeds chosen under Advanced. STANAG 5066 D_PDU framing is read. Tested on simulated signals.

ARQ-E (ARQ-1000 Duplex), receive only: 7-unit ITA2-P characters with inverted characters every 4 or 8; speed, shift, alignment and cycle found automatically. Control characters are counted, not named. Tested on simulated signals.
ARQ-N, receive only: as ARQ-E without inverted characters. Tested on simulated signals.
AUTOSPEC Mk 1, receive only: 10-bit Bauer code on ITA2, single errors corrected. Tested on simulated signals.

SPREAD 11 / 21 / 51, receive only: the Bauer code spread over 11, 21 or 51 bits; the depth is found automatically. The bit layout follows the published description of the spreading. Tested on simulated signals.
G-TOR monitor, receive only: 100, 200, 300 Bd frames with Golay coding and CRC, data and Golay forms both read. ASCII frames show text; Huffman frames stay as hex. Tested on simulated signals.

EFR radio teleswitching, receive only: DCF49 (129.1 kHz) and DCF39 (139 kHz), 200 Bd FSK, DIN 19244 frames with message number, addresses and checksum. Semagyr and Versacom content stays as hex. Tested on simulated signals.
Piccolo Mk VI (II) 6-tone MFSK, receive only: ITA2 by tone pairs at 20 Hz spacing, 50 ms tones. Tested on simulated signals.
Coquelet-8 MFSK, receive only: ITA2 by tone pairs (8 tones, 26.67 Hz spacing), 37.5, 50 or 75 ms tones found automatically. Tested on simulated signals.

QRSS slow Morse (dots of 1 to 120 s): a spectrogram of the narrow window around the keyed tone and the text read from it. The tone and the element length are found automatically; both can be set under Advanced
DFCW dual-frequency slow Morse: all elements are the same length, dots on one frequency and dashes on a second one, with a gap between letters. Spectrogram of the keyed tone and the decoded text

FSK441 meteor scatter (4 tones at 882 / 1323 / 1764 / 2205 Hz, 441 baud, three tones per character): finds the short pings above the noise, the tuning error and the dit timing, and prints what is in them
ISCAT-A and ISCAT-B (WSJT, 42 tones, 24-symbol frames with Costas sync and length symbols) for scatter and aircraft scatter: variant, tuning error and message are found automatically

PI4 (PA0NHC, 4-FSK, 146 symbols of 186 ms, a rate 1/2 K = 32 code, 8 characters): the microwave beacon mode of the 10 GHz and 24 GHz bands; sync, frequency and message are found automatically. A converter brings the band to the radio
Throb and ThrobX (one or two tones at a time out of 9 or 11, symbols of 1, 0.5 or 0.25 s): the tone comb, the variant and the timing are found automatically and the text is printed as it comes

SuperSID: the strength of the VLF navy transmitters (NAA, NLK, NPM, NWC, DHO38, GQD, HWU, ICV ...) from a VLF-capable radio, one value per 5 s, and a mark when a station jumps within ten minutes: the signature of a solar flare in the lower ionosphere

Riometer: cosmic radio noise near 30 MHz measured with interference rejected, compared with a quiet-day curve per sidereal hour, so that ionospheric absorption (a geomagnetic or particle event) shows in dB. Needs a fixed-gain receiver, an antenna looking up and one to two days to build the curve

Pulsar detection: a filter bank, incoherent dedispersion and folding at the period of a chosen pulsar (B0329+54, B0950+08, B1133+16, Crab, Vela ...), with the S/N, a profile and a plain statement of the antenna it needs: about a square metre of effective area with a low-noise amplifier, not a whip

UMTS (3G) cells in a 5 MHz channel, from the synchronisation channels and the pilot: primary scrambling code, code group, Ec/Io, level and carrier offset. Receive only; the broadcast channel (operator and cell identity) is not decoded
Defunct satellites still transmitting (AO-7, Transit 5B-5, LES-1, LES-5, IMAGE): their carriers found and checked by frequency and Doppler
Follows every carrier in the capture and names the satellite whose predicted Doppler curve fits. Needs orbital elements and your location
Skims 240 - 270 MHz military satellite downlinks for active channels (5 and 25 kHz): frequency, width, activity. Detection only
Thuraya GMR-1 satellite phone downlink 1525 - 1559 MHz: active 31.25 kHz channels. No decoder is implemented
Detects Starlink\'s Ku-band downlink by its 750 Hz frame gap (published reverse engineering; no public specification). Needs an LNB and a dish
Detects OneWeb\'s Ku-band downlink by its 1 ms repeating sequence (published reverse engineering; no public specification). Needs an LNB and a dish
NASA TDRS S-band forward links, carrier only (not verified from the ground)
Chinese space station and crew craft: S-band TT&C and telemetry carriers, Doppler checked. The format is not public: carriers only
Russian Transit-type navigation satellites at 150 and 400 MHz. The format is not public: carriers and Doppler only
Russian store-and-forward messaging satellites, 387 - 390 MHz. No public protocol: bursts and channels only
Chinese S-band mobile satellite 2170 - 2200 MHz. No public air interface: channel energy only
Every ISS downlink in one mode: FM voice and SSTV on 145.800, APRS on 145.825, the repeater on 437.800. Shows which is on and opens the decoder
NavIC (IRNSS) L5 at 1176.45 MHz: satellites, time and week number from the navigation message (no position fix). The satellites are receivable around India

Suomi NPP and NOAA-20 direct broadcast (HRD) on 7812 MHz: QPSK 15 Msym/s, CCSDS K=7 r=1/2 with NRZ-M, CADUs, the VIIRS channels and colour composites. Needs a tracking X-band dish (1.2 m or more), a down-converter and 25 Msps or more. A recording is the usual way to use it.

NOAA-21 direct broadcast on 7812 MHz: OQPSK 25 Msym/s, K=7 r=1/2, NRZ-M, 1279-byte CADUs, VIIRS. Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 40 Msps or more. A recording is the usual way to use it.

Aqua and Aura direct broadcast on 8160 MHz: OQPSK 7.5 Msym/s, NRZ-M per rail, the MODIS channels and colour composites (Aqua). Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 15 Msps. A recording is the usual way to use it.

Terra direct broadcast on 8212.5 MHz: BPSK 13.125 Msym/s, K=7 r=1/2, the MODIS channels and colour composites. Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 45 Msps. A recording is the usual way to use it.

MetOp X-band full dump on 7800 MHz: QPSK 35 Msym/s, CADUs, the AVHRR channels of a whole orbit, cloud-top, sea surface and fire maps from the instrument\'s own calibration. Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 45 Msps. A recording is the usual way to use it.

MetOp-SG direct data broadcast on 7825 MHz: QPSK 93.3 Msym/s, CCSDS, the METimage channels. Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 105 Msps or more. A recording is the usual way to use it.

Landsat 8 and 9 X-band link: OQPSK 220.4 Msym/s, TIRS channels from decoded .cadu frames. The LDPC 7/8 code from raw IQ is not decoded here. Needs a tracking X-band dish and 240 Msps or more. A recording is the usual way to use it.
Landsat 8 and 9 S-band link: OQPSK 1.067 Msym/s, K=7 r=1/2, CADU frames. Needs a tracking S-band dish and 2 Msps. A recording is the usual way to use it.

Proba-1, Proba-2 and Proba-V S-band dump on 2235 MHz: BPSK 2 Msym/s, K=7 r=1/2, CADU frames and the Proba-V Vegetation channels. Needs a tracking S-band dish and 3 Msps. A recording is the usual way to use it.

Proba-V X-band dump on 8300 MHz: OQPSK 35 Msym/s, K=7 r=1/2, CADU frames (Vegetation pictures use CCSDS 122 compression, not decoded). Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 38 Msps. A recording is the usual way to use it.

GCOM-W1 X-band link on 8245 MHz: OQPSK 10 Msym/s, K=7 r=1/2, shortened Reed-Solomon, the AMSR2 microwave channels. Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 13 Msps. A recording is the usual way to use it.
GCOM-C1 X-band link: OQPSK 69.4 Msym/s, uncoded CADUs, frame counts only. Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 75 Msps or more. A recording is the usual way to use it.

STEREO A/B high rate on 8443.52 MHz: BPSK 1.44 Msym/s, frame counts from .cadu files. The CCSDS turbo code from raw IQ and the ICER images are not decoded. Needs a large tracking dish (deep space). A recording is the usual way to use it.

Oceansat-2 direct broadcast, X-band: QPSK 21.2 Msym/s, differential, the OCM channels. Tested on simulated signals only. Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 28 Msps. A recording is the usual way to use it.
Oceansat-3 Argos link on 1703 MHz: QPSK 1 Msym/s, K=7 r=1/2, CADU frames. Needs a tracking L-band dish and 1.5 Msps. A recording is the usual way to use it.
Saral Argos link on 1698.4 MHz: QPSK 400 ksym/s, K=7 r=1/2, CADU frames. Needs a tracking L-band dish and 0.6 Msps. A recording is the usual way to use it.
Oceansat-3 X-band dump: QPSK 80 Msym/s, uncoded CADUs with Reed-Solomon, frame counts. Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 90 Msps or more. A recording is the usual way to use it.
Saral X-band dump: QPSK 16 Msym/s, K=7 r=1/2, CADU frames. Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 20 Msps. A recording is the usual way to use it.

Kanopus-V X-band link: QPSK 61.44 Msym/s, differential, the PSS panchromatic swaths and MSS bands. Tested on simulated signals only. Needs a tracking X-band dish, a down-converter and 72 Msps or more. A recording is the usual way to use it.
DMSP real-time data on 2252.5 MHz: BPSK 1.024 Msym/s, the OLS visible and infrared swath. Needs a tracking S-band dish and 2 Msps; works live. A recording is the usual way to use it.
wfb-ng and OpenHD digital video links: 802.11n frames injected in monitor mode, MCS 0 - 7 at 20 MHz. Link and port, FEC block numbers, frames lost; the video stays encrypted
New Packet Radio on 70 cm (F4HDK NPR-70 modems): sync words, network ID and symbol rate of each frame. Frame content is not read, it is whitened by the radio chip. Simulated signals only so far

WINMOR HF frames: the 1500 Hz pilot with tuning error and the raw frame-type tones. The specification does not define the 4FSK symbol mapping, the Reed-Solomon generator or the callsign packing, so frames are detected, not read. Simulated signals only so far

mioty (ETSI TS 103 357 TS-UNB) uplinks: the 24 hopped radio-bursts found and decoded, every uplink TSMA pattern, extension frames. MAC fields shown (address, counter, flags); the payload is encrypted with the network key and stays encrypted. Simulated signals only so far

DECT NR+ (DECT-2020 NR) packets on a 1.728 MHz channel: the physical control field of each packet (network ID, transmitter and receiver IDs, length, MCS, HARQ). Data channel not decoded. Simulated signals only so far

ISDB-TSB (ARIB STD-B29) narrow-band digital sound and data broadcasting: one or three segments, detected from the TMCC; the one-segment receiver also takes the one-seg service of an ISDB-T channel. Three-segment signals with DQPSK segments are unreliable (10-25 % of packets lost). Simulated signals only so far

Futaba S-FHSS 2.4 GHz RC links (CC2500 2-FSK 128 kbit/s, 30 hop channels): transmitter id, hop code and the four channel values of each packet; layout from the DIY-Multiprotocol-TX-Module project, simulated signals only so far. FASST is not decodable (no public description)

Spektrum DSM2 and DSMX 2.4 GHz RC links (CYRF6936 DSSS, 1 Mchip/s): every pn code tried, transmitter id bytes and channel values; DSMX told from DSM2 by the hop channel when the radio\'s frequency is known. The CRC is not checked (not published). Simulated signals only so far

cdma2000 / IS-95 base stations in a 1.25 MHz channel: every pilot by PN offset (Ec/Io, level, carrier offset) and its Sync Channel Message: system and network identity (SID, NID), pilot PN, protocol revision, system time, leap seconds, local time offset, paging channel rate and frequency. Receive only, public broadcast

TD-SCDMA (3G TDD, 1.28 Mcps) cells in a 1.6 MHz channel: the downlink pilot\'s SYNC-DL code (code group), the cell parameter (scrambling code and midamble) from time slot 0, the frame parity and P-CCPCH position from the SYNC-DL phases, level and carrier offset. Receive only; the broadcast channel is not decoded

JT6M 6 m scatter (44 tones 21.5 Hz apart from 1076.66 Hz, 21.5 baud, a sync tone every third symbol): finds the pings, the tuning error and the frame timing, lists the characters of each ping and folds a long signal into its repeating message

VDL Mode 3: TDMA D8PSK voice and data link on 118 to 137 MHz (ICAO Annex 10; trialled, never deployed; synthetic + spec; receive only). Burst kinds, Golay and Reed-Solomon checked, data octets; the system data and headers as raw values (ICAO Doc 9805 is not public), voice not decoded

Meteosat high rate data collection platforms (HRDCP, EUMETSAT TD 16) on the 402.2 - 402.435 MHz regional band: a 2 s carrier, then the message at 1200 bit/s offset QPSK with a convolutional code (r = 1/2, K = 7), the CCSDS randomiser, Reed-Solomon (255,223) frames and a CRC-32. Every carrier in the capture is followed; the BCH-protected platform address, the channel, the sequence counter, alert or self-timed, the health bits and the platform data (ASCII, pseudo-binary or binary) are shown, with a table of the platforms heard and a CSV log. Needs a radio that covers 402.2 - 402.435 MHz (0.25 Msps or more) and a UHF antenna

DVB-SH (ETSI EN 302 583) mobile TV in the OFDM form SH-A: 1K / 2K / 4K / 8K, QPSK or 16-QAM (also hierarchical), the 3GPP2 turbo code and the long time interleaver, parameters from the TPS, channel width found automatically (5, 8, 7, 6, 1.7 MHz); and the TDM satellite form SH-B (QPSK, 8PSK, 16APSK, symbol rate found from the standard\'s table). Simulated signals only so far

STANAG 4539 / MIL-STD-188-110C Appendix C high-rate HF modem, receive only: 2400 Bd on 1800 Hz, 3200 to 12800 bit/s (QPSK, 8-PSK, 16/32/64-QAM). Speed and interleaver are read from the preamble, which is also found in the middle of a transmission; a decision-feedback equaliser computed from the channel measured on every mini-probe, so multipath channels such as ITU-R Poor (2 ms, 1 Hz fading) decode; deinterleaver and tail-biting Viterbi decoding, the end-of-message pattern, STANAG 5066 D_PDU framing when present. Tested on simulated signals.

3G-ALE (MIL-STD-188-141B Appendix C, the link setup of STANAG 4538), receive only: BW0 bursts of 8-PSK at 2400 Bd on 1800 Hz, found from their preamble at any time; Walsh symbols, deinterleaver and Viterbi decoding, the CRC of each PDU, then LE_Call, LE_Handshake, LE_Notification and LE_Broadcast in words. Also the traffic bursts: BW1 (TM link requests, confirms and terminations, HDL acknowledgements), BW2 (HDL data packets), BW3 (LDL data packets) and BW4 (LDL acknowledgements), with the packets put back together into datagrams. Tested on simulated signals.

Link 11 CLEW (the conventional 16-tone HF waveform), receive only, frame structure only: each message is found from its 605 Hz Doppler and 2915 Hz sync tones, then the frame rate (13.33 or 22 ms), the Doppler offset, the number of frames and the raw phase changes of the 15 data tones. The bit mapping, error code and addresses are not public, so no data is shown. Link 11 SLEW is not covered. Tested on simulated signals.

STANAG 4481 naval HF broadcast, FSK part, receive only: single-channel RATT with a +-425 Hz shift, or up to 16 sub-carriers at 255 + 170 n Hz shifted +-42.5 Hz, found automatically. Each channel\'s speed is measured; plain ITA2 text is shown, encrypted (synchronous) channels only by speed and bit count. The PSK part of STANAG 4481 is STANAG 4285, its own mode. Tested on simulated signals.

DVB-C2 cable TV (EN 302 769): 4K OFDM, guard interval 1/64 or 1/128, the L1 signalling, Data Slice Types 1 and 2, 16 to 4096-QAM with 16K and 64K LDPC, transport streams and GSE (IP); needs a cable feed. Simulated signals only so far

Russian Navy BEE (T-600) 2-FSK, receive only: idle reversals at 36 or 50 Bd and traffic at 50 or 100 Bd (75 and 150 Bd too), shift and polarity found automatically. The 44-bit start word, the 70-bit session key sent twice, the 7-bit 3:4 characters and the end-of-message are read and shown as hex. The traffic is encrypted: nothing is decrypted. Simulated signals only so far

CIS-14 (AMOR, AMOR96) 2-FSK at 96 Bd, receive only: the 14-bit frame is found from its period and every frame\'s fields are shown raw (2 state bits, two 5-bit code words, 2 parity bits). The parity rule and the state codes are not published, so they are shown, not checked. Simulated signals only so far

CIS-12 (MS5, AT-3004D, AT-3104D, FIRE, T-230), receive only, physical layer: the 3300 Hz pilot and its offset, the 12 carriers 700 - 2900 Hz at 120 Bd, the PSK order (DBPSK / DQPSK) and the raw phase steps of every carrier. No frame format is published, so nothing further is read. Simulated signals only so far

CIS-36 MFSK duplex ARQ, identification only: the tone count, the 40 Hz spacing, the 10 / 20 / 40 Bd tone rate and the tone groups are measured and the signal named. No frame format is published. Simulated signals only so far

CIS OFDM HDR modem (CIS-45, CIS-60, CIS-93), identification only: the OFDM symbol (useful part, guard, rate), the carrier count and the PSK order are measured and the variant named. No frame format is published. Simulated signals only so far

CIS-128, identification only: about 128 OFDM carriers at about 21 Bd in 3 kHz, from the carrier spacing, the symbol rate and the guard. The 6 kHz form is not covered. No frame format is published. Simulated signals only so far
CIS-3000, identification only: a single carrier 8-PSK at 3000 Bd, from its symbol-rate line and the constellation order. No frame format is published. Simulated signals only so far

Lightning position (network): several OnAir stations with radios time the same sferic; one acts as the server, collects the detections and finds the strike by time difference of arrival. Each station shows which timing source it uses (GPS-disciplined radio time, a GNSS receiver, a common-view VLF / LF transmitter, or PTP / NTP for association only) and its estimated error; the server draws the strikes with error ellipses on the map. Authenticated with a network key, off until set up, nothing relayed elsewhere. Receive only

GOMspace NanoCom AX100 Mode 5 from amateur satellites on 70 cm: GMSK / FSK at 9600 or 4800 bit/s, the sync word 0x930B51DE, a Golay (24,12) coded length, CCSDS scrambler and Reed-Solomon (255,223), CSP packets with the header decoded. The CubeSat telemetry decoder showing this framing only (it also runs inside CubeSat telemetry)

GOMspace NanoCom AX100 Mode 6 from amateur satellites on 70 cm: a Reed-Solomon (255,223) coded CSP packet inside an HDLC frame, G3RUH scrambled, 9600 bit/s. The CubeSat telemetry decoder showing this framing only (it also runs inside CubeSat telemetry)

SPUTNIX USP (Universal Space Protocol) from Russian amateur and cubesat transmitters on 70 cm: FSK at 9600 bit/s, the USP frame with its CRC. The CubeSat telemetry decoder showing this framing only (it also runs inside CubeSat telemetry)

NGHam (Next Generation Ham radio protocol, FloripaSat and other cubesats) on 70 cm: GMSK / FSK frames with Reed-Solomon and CRC. The CubeSat telemetry decoder showing this framing only (it also runs inside CubeSat telemetry)

GOMspace U482C (GomX-1 and similar) on 70 cm: AFSK at 4800 bit/s on a 3600 Hz audio carrier, scrambled and Reed-Solomon coded frames. The CubeSat telemetry decoder showing this framing only (it also runs inside CubeSat telemetry)

BEESAT-1 / BEESAT-9 and other TU Berlin and TECHNOSAT cubesats on 70 cm: Mobitex-NX blocks with Mobitex CRCs at 4800 bit/s GMSK. The CubeSat telemetry decoder showing this framing only (it also runs inside CubeSat telemetry)
